title: VPC fundamentals in one screen
rememberThis: A VPC is your private network; subnets are AZ-scoped slices with their own route table association.
Public subnet = route 0.0.0.0/0 to Internet Gateway. Private subnet = no direct IGW route; use NAT for outbound.
NAT Gateway sits in a public subnet and uses an Elastic IP — deploy one per AZ so AZ failure does not kill all egress.
VPC DNS resolver is at the VPC network address plus two (e.g. 10.0.0.2 for 10.0.0.0/16).
Production pattern: multi-AZ public subnets for ALB and NAT, multi-AZ private subnets for compute and data.
bullets: Do not put databases in public subnets — no inbound internet path needed, shrink blast radius.
Default VPC is fine for labs; production needs explicit CIDR planning and flow logs.
Security groups are stateful; network ACLs are stateless subnet fences — both matter.
Stopping an EC2 instance releases its ephemeral public IP unless an Elastic IP is attached.
Route table local route (VPC CIDR → local) is implicit and cannot be deleted.

rows.label: VPC CIDR
rows.value: Private IP range for the entire network (e.g. 10.0.0.0/16)

rows.label: Subnet
rows.value: AZ-bound slice; public or private by routing intent, not by name alone

rows.label: IGW
rows.value: Internet-facing gateway attached to the VPC for public traffic

rows.label: NAT GW
rows.value: Managed outbound translation for private subnet instances

rows.label: Route table
rows.value: Routing rules; each subnet links to exactly one

rows.label: Elastic IP
rows.value: Static public IPv4 you control until released
